content: Interviewers report that recent fresh graduate candidates possess impressive resumes and surface-level AI knowledge, yet struggle with foundational concepts like tokenization and inference mechanisms. The author attributes this to an academic environment reliant on AI for education and research, which fosters a cycle of rote memorization rather than deep understanding. Consequently, many candidates exhibit a "half-understood" state, confident in jargon but lacking technical depth. This widespread phenomenon creates a paradox of high performance with significant underlying knowledge gaps, highlighting the need for better foundational education in the AI era.

content: Google has globally launched its flagship Gemini 4 Carbon AI model, accessible via API and various platforms. The system achieves top rankings in multiple benchmarks and introduces a multi-agent swarm feature capable of complex tasks like 3D architectural reconstruction and massive code verification. It also offers an affordable pricing structure, significantly reducing per-task costs compared to competitors. Additionally, Google is providing six months of free access to ten thousand global scientists to facilitate advanced research in fields ranging from physics to climate science.

title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
content: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s Web Search API provides agents with current, cited results using existing AWS credentials, eliminating third-party dependencies. This tutorial demonstrates building a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph. The system researches package ecosystems in parallel, enforcing strict constraints like date windows and source blocklists in code. It verifies findings against retrieved sources and filters duplicates using a state store. The solution runs on AWS Lambda or AgentCore Runtime, with AgentCore Gateway offering centralized policy management for multi-team environments.
